newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end limit down after cattle report.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end limit down after cattle report.

text.p: A bearish monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report Friday continued to pressure CME live cattle futures and October ended down the daily 1.500 cent-per-lb limit as fund liquidation added to losses.
Concern over a recall of hamburger by one U.S. company because of the possiblity of E-coli contamination, added to the bearish tone, traders said.

Live cattle closed off 1.500 to 0.425 cent per lb with October off limit at 68.700 cents, a 3-1/2 week low. December was also fell down the limit before ending off 1.400 at 70.775 cents. Feeders finished 0.775 to 0.200 cent a lb lower with October off 0.650 at 80.275 cents
The USDA cattle data weighed on futures from the start.

"The Cattle-on-Feed was one of the most bearish reports we had in some time, with the placements up and well above trade expectations," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management.

The report showed July placements onto feed in key U.S. states at 118 percent of a year earlier, sharply above the high end of expectations of 106.5 percent. This put on-feed supplies at 119 percent of a year earlier, above the high end of estimates of 117.8 percent.
"I think we are still placing cattle in August and the cattle that were placed in July were fairly heavy" which is bearish for October and December futures, Skold said.

Concern over E.coli in hamburger meat added to the bearish sentiment. The USDA announced Friday the largest recall of U.S. ground beef products in history due to potential contamination by E.coli bacteria. Hudson Foods Inc is recalling 1.2 million lbs of frozen beef patties after 16 people in Colorado became sick from eating the beef in June.
But most traders did not expect any long term effects on futures from the recall and generally attributed Monday's losses to the cattle report and fund technical selling on the setback.
"I don't expect any long lasting things from the E.coli," Skold added.

Cargill Investor Services notably sold October early while R.J. O'Brien, RBH, Dean Witter, Prudential Securities and Refco sold late, traders said. In live cattle options, commercials bought December 70 puts early and commission houses sold the December strangle, selling 68 puts and 73 calls late, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle followed the lead of live cattle but were also influenced by corn futures at times. Feeders showed support when corn futures were lower but faded when corn futures moved higher, traders said.

Lind-Waldock and LIT division of First Options pressured October while locals sold back months. RBH and E.D.&F. Man bought September while spreaders bought October and sold September. Spreaders also boght April live cattle and sold November feeders, pit sources said.

Boneless beef futures were under pressure from liquidation sparked by the E.coli concerns, with August setting a new low and October down the daily limit of 2.00 cents a lb early on a single trade. August set a new low of 90.50 cents. Trimmings were also down in light trade, traders said.
Boneless beef closed 1.50 to 0.10 cent lower with August off most at 90.50 cents. Trimmings were 0.70 to 0.40 lower with August off most at 42.80 cents.
